t: Metadata Reconstruction Tool: a plain-language overview (Signature)
title: Metadata Reconstruction Tool: a plain-language overview (Signature)
description: Signature record. Overview: what the Metadata Reconstruction Tool does and why archives need it. Signature original. The Signature reconstruction method treats every clue as evidence with a weight: a filename hint, an embedded tag, a manifest row — each stamped with where it was found. Stronger evidence outranks weaker, and anything below the honesty threshold is recorded as unknown. The archive never invents a date.
provenance: Signature-authored original method by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Property of Justin Addam Higgins.

t: How the Metadata Reconstruction Tool works (Signature)
title: How the Metadata Reconstruction Tool works (Signature)
description: Signature record. Overview: what the Metadata Reconstruction Tool does and why archives need it. Signature original. The Signature approach builds an evidence ledger per file: each candidate fact (date, author, title, event) becomes a ledger entry with its source, its extraction rule, and a deterministic confidence weight. A fixed priority order — embedded properties, then manifests, then filename patterns, then folder context — resolves conflicts the same way every run. Re-running reconstruction on the same collection reproduces the identical merged records, making the whole process auditable. This is a Signature-authored method, original to Justin Addam Higgins.
provenance: Signature-authored original method by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Property of Justin Addam Higgins.
